name: ROS 2 tf2 transform listener and turtle-following node
summary: Official ROS geometry tutorial node that spawns turtle2, looks up its transform relative to a target frame and publishes Twist velocity commands to follow that target. It is an installed ROS 2 console entrypoint with ROS graph effects, not a direct Python-file main or a verified robot controller.

license.scope: Selected listener source under its explicit Apache-2.0 header, copyright 2021 Open Source Robotics Foundation, Inc. Preserve attribution, license and applicable notices. The package also declares BSD for other material; this source review does not clear the full package, dependencies or physical-robot use.

packages: Compatible ROS 2 rclpy environment with the context-manager init API used by this source
Installed turtle_tf2_py package exposing the reviewed console entrypoint
system: Configured ROS graph providing the relative spawn service and appropriate turtle1/turtle2 transforms
Reviewed namespace, target_frame parameter and intended turtle2/cmd_vel subscribers
requirements.notes: The package is labeled version 0.7.0 at a Rolling-branch source pin; neither label establishes a tested ROS distribution, Python version or operating system. The node defaults target_frame to turtle1, requests turtle2 at x=4.0, y=2.0, theta=0.0 and, after spawning, queries a transform into turtle2 with rclpy.time.Time(). On a nominal one-second timer it publishes angular z from atan2 and linear x as 0.5 times translation distance. The period and gains are source settings, not measurements. Transform failures are logged and return without an explicit zero-velocity stop. No obstacle check or speed clamp is present. This node does not generate its required transforms, and a single source file is insufficient. ROS graph dependencies, shutdown behavior, hardware remappings and compatibility remain untested.

invocation.notes: Installed ROS 2 console command backed by the pinned setup.py registration turtle_tf2_py.turtle_tf2_listener:main. The source defines main without a __main__ guard; direct python-file execution is not the declared node invocation. Starting the console entrypoint initializes rclpy, calls a spawn service and can publish velocity commands to the configured graph. No physical-controller compatibility or safe stopping is established. The Hub supplies inert source metadata with no preparation/execution adapter and ran no ROS node or simulator.

access.instructions: Read the pinned node, package declarations and setup registration before configuring the intended ROS graph. This source reference does not install or execute code.

evidence.inspection: Complete node read as inert text and Python AST parsed without import or execution. Source, license, package XML and setup bytes matched SHA-256, lengths and immutable-tree Git blob pins. Installed console registration and ROS graph effects were inspected; no ROS/Python/OS combination, controller, simulator or task result was tested.
